business-api-context

Bunkai API map

The business story of the Bunkai TMS API. Not an endpoint catalog: the contract is public/openapi.json in ../upex-bunkai-tms, and paths here are relative to that repo; openapi:<tag> names a contract tag.

Overview

The Bunkai API lets a QA team do through HTTP everything it does in the browser: build the traceable chain from user story to ATC to Test, execute runs and report step results, file and move bugs, sign off test plans, and administer the workspace. The same endpoints serve the web app (cookie session) and agents or CI pipelines (Personal Access Token), and the design goal is that both behave identically.

The API is a thin gateway. Each route validates input with zod, resolves who is calling, checks the capability the route declares, then calls a bunkai_* Postgres function under Row Level Security. Business rules (state transitions, limits, consistency) live in those functions, so an API test exercises the real rule, and a UI test adds only the UI on top.

Contract: public/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1, generated from the route schemas, served live at /api/openapi with docs at /api/docs). Servers: local, staging (https://staging-upexbunkai.vercel.app) and production. This map tells what the groups mean; the contract holds every request and response.

Permission and auth model

TierWhoHow to acquireWhere enforced
PublicAnyonenothingroute posture public: auth endpoints, health, invite accept, Stripe webhook (signature only)
Cookie session (cookieAuth)Browser userssign in on /login; Supabase writes sb-…-auth-tokenlib/api/principal.ts; cookie-only routes (token mint and revoke, workspace restore) refuse a PAT
Bearer PAT (bearerAuth)Agents, CI, scriptsPOST /auth/signin (returns a PAT) or POST /tokens from a browserlib/api/middleware/bearer.ts, lib/api/pat.ts
CapabilityAny authenticated callerPAT scopes atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin; a cookie session holds allroute requires: [...] in withApiHandler
Workspace roleMembersinvite and acceptSQL: bunkai_is_workspace_member, bunkai_can_write_workspace, bunkai_is_workspace_admin, bunkai_is_workspace_owner inside RLS and RPCs
System (cronAuth)Vercel cronCRON_SECRET bearer, never issued to usersapp/api/v1/admin/*

Two checks stack: the capability (does this token allow writes?) and the role (may this person write in this workspace?). A member's PAT with only atc:read gets 403 on a write; a viewer's cookie session passes the capability check and then fails in SQL with 42501, also 403. Default PAT scopes exclude workspace:admin, and a PAT cannot mint another PAT.

Error semantics

Every error uses one envelope with a machine code, a message and the x-request-id header. Postgres raises custom SQLSTATEs; each domain's lib/<domain>/errors.ts maps them to an API code and status (there is no central table, and number ranges overlap between domains, so map by call site).

StatusMeaning in BunkaiExamples
400Malformed body or query (zod)missing field, wrong type
401No valid identity; uniform for every token problemexpired, revoked, unknown PAT
403Identity is fine but not allowedmissing capability; viewer write (42501); PAT on a cookie-only route
404Not found or not visible (RLS hides other workspaces' rows as 404)P0002; archived ATC by id
409State conflictrun already closed (45204, 45206, 45212); different step re-report (45239); closed plan edit; sole owner
413 · 415Evidence upload limitsfile_too_large, unsupported_media_type
422Business rule refusedno executable steps (45202), bug status skip or backward (45310, 45311), empty chain (45120), project limit
429Rate limitedauth endpoints
503Dependency not configuredpayment_processor_unavailable, storage_unavailable

QA consequence: "not found" for another workspace's object is correct behaviour (no existence leak), and the same rule refused through the UI and the API must return the same code.

Journey: headless sign-in and token use

How an agent or a test suite gets an identity without email steps (security-critical: every automated journey starts here).

  1. POST /auth/signin with a confirmed account returns a session and a fresh PAT (why: lets CI start without a browser; ADR-0027 in this repo uses it).
  2. The PAT is sent as Bearer on every call; the gateway resolves the owner and scopes.
  3. Tokens are listed with GET /tokens; revoking (DELETE /tokens/{id}) needs a browser session, so a leaked PAT cannot revoke others.

Endpoints: POST /api/v1/auth/signin, GET /api/v1/tokens, POST /api/v1/tokens, DELETE /api/v1/tokens/{id}.

Entities: flow-membership (roles), state-jobs (idempotency). Features: feature-auth, feature-integrations (FEAT-082).

Journey: execute a run

The core value of the product: turn a Test into recorded results (highest data risk; every report reads them).

  1. Create the run with a Test, an environment and a start_token; replaying the same token within 24 h returns the same run (safe retry).
  2. The RPC snapshots the ATC chain, so later ATC edits never rewrite this run.
  3. Mark steps; each mark recomputes the ATC result and stamps the idle clock.
  4. Upload evidence in two calls (create pending, then commit) so half-uploaded files never count.
  5. Finish with the caller's verdict, or abort with a reason; leftovers become skipped and the executor is notified.

Endpoints: POST /api/v1/runs, POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/mark, POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/attachments, POST …/attachments/{attachmentId}/commit, POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/finish, POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/abort, GET /api/v1/runs/{id}.

Entities: flow-manual-run, state-runs, state-run-results, flow-evidence-upload. Features: feature-runs (FEAT-040, FEAT-042).

Journey: agent or CI result submission

Lets a pipeline report a finished execution in one call (the product's automation differentiator).

  1. POST /runs/submissions with the verdict and every step result; the run is stored already closed as agent.
  2. The database refuses a verdict that contradicts the steps (45235) and dedupes resubmissions through submission keys.
  3. Alternatively stream: create, mark, finish; an agent or CI run idle for 60 minutes is aborted by the sweep.

Endpoints: POST /api/v1/runs/submissions, POST /api/v1/runs, POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/mark.

Entities: flow-automated-run-submission. Features: feature-runs (FEAT-043).

Journey: file and move a bug

Keeps defects inside the test cycle, anchored to the module, run step and ATC that found them.

  1. POST /bugs with module, severity and optionally run, run step and ATC; a trigger rejects anchors that cross projects.
  2. Assign through /assign (active non-viewer members only).
  3. Move status through /status one step forward; notifications go to reporter and assignee.

Endpoints: POST /api/v1/bugs, POST /api/v1/bugs/{id}/assign, POST /api/v1/bugs/{id}/status, GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/bugs/heatmap.

Entities: flow-bug-lifecycle, state-bugs. Features: feature-bugs.

Journey: upgrade to Cloud

The only journey where money changes hands (revenue).

  1. Checkout creates an open session row, then a Stripe Checkout Session, and returns its URL.
  2. Stripe calls the webhook; the signature is verified on the raw body (bad or missing = 400).
  3. The plan becomes cloud only for a paid session; duplicates are ignored; an unknown session returns 5xx so Stripe retries.
  4. Later invoices drive the payment state and the 14-day grace window; /billing/retry and /payment-method recover.

Endpoints: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout, POST …/billing/checkout/cancel, POST /api/v1/billing/webhook, GET …/billing, GET …/billing/invoices, POST …/billing/retry.

Entities: flow-billing-upgrade, state-billing. Features: feature-integrations (FEAT-080).

Journey: invite and accept a member

A permission change: who can see and write a workspace (security).

  1. Admin or owner creates the invite (workspace:admin); the token is emailed, only its hash is stored.
  2. The invitee accepts with the token while signed in; the RPC re-checks the inviter's current rank.
  3. Resend rotates the token; delete revokes it.

Endpoints: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/invites, GET /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/invites, POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/invites/{inviteId}, DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/invites/{inviteId}, POST /api/v1/invites/accept, DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/members/{userId}.

Entities: flow-membership, state-membership. Features: feature-workspace (FEAT-011).

Journey: delete, restore and export a workspace

Highest blast radius: one call removes a whole tenant's access.

  1. DELETE /workspaces/{id} (owner) soft-deletes: every member loses access at once and a restore email goes out.
  2. POST /workspaces/{id}/restore (owner, browser session) within 30 days.
  3. Export before deleting: request, poll, download while unexpired.

Endpoints: DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}, POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/restore, POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/data-export, GET /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/data-export, GET …/data-export/download.

Entities: flow-workspace-deletion, flow-workspace-export. Features: feature-workspace (FEAT-012, FEAT-013).

Architecture behind the API

ComponentRoleTouchesWhy it matters for QA
withApiHandler (lib/api/handler.ts)Validation, principal, capability, error envelope, request id, idempotencyidempotency_keysOne place where posture bugs show; a posture scanner test enforces every route declares one
Principal resolutionBearer PAT first, else cookie; mints a 60 s user JWTaccess_tokensCookie and PAT must give the same result (lib/api/rls-parity.test.ts)
bunkai_* RPCsBusiness rules, transitions, cascadesall tablesWhere 409 and 422 come from
RLS policiesRow visibility per roleall tablesCross-workspace access returns 404, not 403
Service-role clientBypasses RLS for webhook, crons, auth, imports, idempotencyvariousBugs here bypass tenancy; worth targeted tests
Supabase StorageEvidence and exports, private bucketsrun-evidence, workspace-exportsUpload limits and two-step commit
Vercel serverlessHosting; crons only in productionDigest and cleanup cannot be observed on staging without calling admin routes

Discovery gaps

  • The Stripe webhook (/api/v1/billing/webhook) is not in the OpenAPI contract; its behaviour comes from code and migrations.
  • The contract marks no operation as public (no empty security); public routes are known from the route postures, not the spec.
  • Project read, update and delete have no API endpoint; the UI uses server pages and actions that were not traced.
  • Delete endpoints are absent for tests, test plans, milestones and bugs; whether the UI offers delete through server actions was not verified.
  • The data-export permission (owner or admin) was not confirmed.
  • Cookie-to-PAT parity was taken from the existence of lib/api/rls-parity.test.ts, not re-run.
  • The service-role client is imported by 77 route files; not every use was reviewed for tenancy leaks.
  • Journeys were capped at 7; import, plan sign-off and chat were left to the e2e map.
  • The legacy .context/business/business-api-map.md (2026-08-24) in the product repo was used as input only.
